audit.why: Level chart in full (phases[].side) and content (win[]) already agree with each other and with the mirrored galio__tryndamere audit: Tryndamere, Skill, Galio, Galio, Galio, Tryndamere, Tryndamere. The packet levelChart disagrees but the mirror is authoritative and already audited.
audit.corrected: Tryndamere, Skill, Galio, Galio, Galio, Tryndamere, Tryndamere.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text gave no cooldown numbers for either kit.
audit.why: Galio: Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7s, Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14s, Winds of War 11/10/9/8/7s, Hero's Entrance 180/160/140s. Tryndamere: Spinning Slash 12/11/10/9/8s, Bloodlust 12s, Undying Rage 120/100/80s for 5s.
audit.corrected: His W is on 18s at rank 1 and his E on 11s — those two gaps are your commit windows. Hero's Entrance is a 180s roam tool at rank 1, not a duel button.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Undying Rage casts through cast-inhibiting CC, so Shield of Durand's taunt does not deny your 5 seconds.
audit.why: Verified from the mirrored Galio audit; restated from Tryndamere's side.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage casts through his taunt — his only lockdown cannot stop your survival window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield of Durand was described as flat damage reduction; it is far weaker against you specifically.
audit.why: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% and physical exactly half that (12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%). Tryndamere is pure physical, so it blunts him far less than the text implies. Also the taunt lands on release, not on the charge.
audit.corrected: His W cuts your physical damage only 12.5% at rank 1 — it is a taunt threat, not a damage wall.

audit.why: Galio's passive is an empowered auto with a visible wind-up; the swing, not a cast bar, is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: Step back on Colossal Smash's wind-up, not on an ability cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named only a generic 'committal tool'.
audit.why: Justice Punch is both his engage and his only escape; when it is spent he has 11s with no exit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Common Mistakes repeated the don'ts verbatim.
audit.why: Replaced one generic line with the passive-tell mistake players actually make.

edits.before: Galio's Winds of War (Q) poke and Shield of Durand (W) damage-reduction make levels 4-5 his window — he can zone you and tank your trades behind W. Don't walk into his Q double-tornado; wait for W to be down, then E in and Q crit before he can charge Durand's taunt.
edits.after: Shield of Durand cuts physical damage only half as hard as magic — 12.5% at rank 1, 22.5% at rank 5 — so his W is a taunt threat, not a wall. It charges up to 1.5s before release: step out of its 350 range while he holds it, then E in and crit on its 18s cooldown.

edits.before: Galio's ult is a global roam tool, not a lane-kill button, so at 6 the lane control swings back to you. With full Fury and Undying Rage you all-in through his W and Justice Punch (E) knock-up. Track when his R is used to roam and punish the side lane before he returns.
edits.after: Undying Rage casts through his taunt — CC does not stop it, so his W cannot deny your 5 seconds of survival. Hero's Entrance is a 180s roam tool, not a lane-kill button: all-in at 6 with full Fury, and when he flies bot, take the side lane before he lands back.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Galio's window — his Q zoning and W damage reduction let him win trades and control the wave. Respect his taunt setup and only commit when W is down. At 6 the lane swings back to you: his ult is a roam tool, not a duel button, and your Undying Rage all-in beats his kit.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Galio's window — Winds of War zones the wave and Shield of Durand blunts your trades, though it cuts physical only half as much as magic. Commit when W is down; its taunt lands on release, not on the charge. At 6 your Undying Rage all-in beats his roaming ult.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash + knockup engage. Punish him when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Justice Punch (E): 11s at rank 1, his only escape and his knockup — engage the moment it is spent. - Shield of Durand (W): 18s, and the taunt only lands on release. - Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1, 5 seconds — kill windows only.

edits.before: His dash + knockup engage. Punish him when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Justice Punch is his engage and his only exit — 11s at rank 1. Spin in the moment he spends it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Step out of its 650 range while it is up; he has 11s of nothing then.

edits.before: Track Galio's Justice Punch: His dash + knockup engage. Punish him when it's down. When it is down — Spin in, crit him down.
edits.after: Undying Rage casts through Shield of Durand's taunt, so his lockdown never stops your 5 seconds — spend them killing him.

edits.before: Trade at zero fury. Eat his Justice Punch for free. Burn R before the burst. Don't spend your ultimate on chip — it is the kill window.
edits.after: Trading at zero fury. Facing Colossal Smash's charged auto instead of stepping back. Burning Undying Rage before the burst rather than into it.

notes: Kit flag misfire: Galio's Justice Punch carries a 'terrain' flag, but Riot's description is a step-back charge that knocks up the first champion hit — it creates no terrain. The missingInteractions headline 'Galio can cut your retreat with Justice Punch' is built on that bad flag and was not written to the page.
